title: Remote vs Office Calculator: Is Remote Work Worth It?
description: Calculate the true financial value of remote work vs office. Factor in commute savings, rent arbitrage, food costs, and reclaimed time.

inputs.name: commuteCost
inputs.label: Annual Avoidable Commute Cash Cost (5 office days/week)

inputs.name: rentDifference
inputs.label: Monthly Rent Savings (if remote allows cheaper area)

inputs.name: foodCoffeeCost
inputs.label: Extra Food/Coffee Spending per Office Day

methodSummary: Avoided commuting = five-day annual commute cash cost × remote days / 5.
Food savings = extra office food spending × remote days × 48 weeks.
Cash savings = avoided commuting + food savings + annual rent savings − additional home office costs.
Time value = daily round-trip hours × remote days × 48 × your hourly value.
assumptions: A five-day work week and 48 commuting weeks per year.
Include only vehicle costs you can actually avoid. A car payment may continue even on remote days.
Rent savings and home office costs are full scenario amounts, applied when remote days exceed zero. Enter zero rent savings unless you actually move.
insights: With three remote days, 60% of the five-day commuting cash cost is avoided.
A lower gross salary needs an after-tax comparison; do not equate personal time value with spendable income.

faqs.a: Yes. Remote days scale commuting, food savings and saved time.

faqs.q: What food amount should I enter?
faqs.a: Enter office spending minus what the same food would cost at home.
Only include them if the change actually eliminates the expense.
Enter the monthly saving for your actual planned home. It is not scaled by remote days.
No. It is a personal valuation shown separately from cash.
Include the annual amount you expect to spend, plus additional utilities, less reimbursements.

richContent:
Worked example: three remote days

Suppose five office days cost $3,000 a year in avoidable travel, office meals cost $15 more per day, and there are 48 work weeks. Three remote days save $1,800 in travel and $2,160 in meals. With no rent change and $600 of added home costs, cash savings are $3,360. Saving 1.5 hours on each remote day recovers 216 hours; at a personal $25/hour, that adds $5,400 of time value. The combined $8,760 is not an $8,760 increase in take-home pay.

Run the example again with zero time value before considering a pay cut. Then compare actual benefits and estimated after-tax salaries using your offer documents.
quickAnswer: Remote work saves money only when avoided costs exceed added costs. Compare cash savings separately from the personal value of your saved commute time.
resultNote: Cash savings are spending reductions, not a gross salary raise. Time value is subjective and cannot pay bills. Taxes, benefit differences and moving costs are excluded.
